meta.subtitle: A clean beat-and-raise quarter, but at $193.00 the shares already sit above the Street's $179.36 consensus target

analystCommentary:
Qualys printed a solid Q2'26 (quarter ended June 30, 2026): revenue of $182.2M grew {+ 11% +} year over year, GAAP operating margin reached 34%, and management raised full-year revenue guidance to $732.0–$738.0 million from $721.0–$727.0 million. Nothing in the quarter argues against the business.

The question is price. At $193.00 the stock trades near the top of its $74.51 – $201.54 52-week range and above the $179.36 consensus target, with 17 of 22 analysts at Hold. The raised guide still implies 9% to 10% growth for 2026, and the Q3 revenue guide carries the same 9% to 10% range, below the Q2 growth rate. That is a durable, profitable compounder growing at roughly a tenth a year, and the current valuation already pays for it.

We rate the shares **HOLD** with a $180–$205 target range. Our Base case is today's price; the upside path needs the reacceleration management talks about to show up in reported revenue, and the downside path is a real one if growth slips below the guide. We would revisit on a Q3 print above the guided range or on a pullback toward the lower half of the Street's target range.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Qualys, Inc. sells cloud-based IT, security and compliance solutions on its Enterprise TruRisk Platform: vulnerability management, detection and response, cybersecurity asset management, patch management, policy audit, endpoint detection and response, and the TotalCloud cloud-native application protection platform. The company was incorporated in 1999 and is headquartered in Foster City, California. Its August 4, 2026 press release describes more than 10,000 subscription customers worldwide.

The model is software-as-a-service on renewable, mostly one-year subscriptions. Per the 10-Q MD&A, Qualys generally invoices the full subscription at the start of the term, carries it as deferred revenue, and recognizes it ratably. It sells through a field sales force to enterprises and government, an inside sales force to smaller businesses, and a channel of managed security service providers, cloud providers, resellers and consulting firms. The company reports a single segment.

thesis.body:
- **Quality is not in question.** GAAP operating margin has widened each year from 21.3% in FY21 to 33.2% in FY25, and free cash flow funds both investment and buybacks (see Financials).
- **Growth is the constraint.** Revenue growth slowed after FY22 and has run near 10% in FY24 and FY25; the raised 2026 guide still implies 9% to 10%.
- **The price already discounts the quality.** The stock trades above the Street's consensus target and at a forward multiple that, on what looks like a non-GAAP EPS basis, leaves little room for disappointment (see Valuation).
- **HOLD.** Our Base case sits at the current price; we need evidence of reacceleration, not just management's stated confidence, before moving higher.

catalysts: Q3'26 results against the $185.5–$187.5 million revenue guide; a print above the range would test the reacceleration narrative (see Growth).
Federal traction after TotalCloud's FedRAMP High Authorization, which management ties to a growing federal pipeline.
Early commercial evidence from QFlex and Enterprise TruRisk Management adoption, both cited by the CEO as demand signals.
risks: Growth stalls below the guided range, removing the support for the current multiple (see Risks).
Price competition in a market the 10-K calls intense and price-sensitive pressures renewals and gross margin.
Macro-driven budget scrutiny and extended sales cycles, which the 10-Q MD&A flags, slow new business.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue reached $669.1M in FY25, up {+ 10.1% +}. The growth rate decelerated from +19.1% in FY22 to +13.2% in FY23 and +9.6% in FY24 before ticking back up in FY25. Profitability has moved the other way: gross margin rose in each year of the table, from 78.2% in FY21 to 82.8% in FY25, and operating margin widened in each year from 21.3% to 33.2%. Diluted EPS climbed every year, from $1.77 in FY21 to $5.44 in FY25.

Q2'26 continued the pattern. GAAP operating income rose {+ 20% +} to $61.9 million, taking operating margin to 34% from 31% a year earlier, and GAAP diluted EPS was $1.50 against $1.29. The press release does not explain the margin gain.

The GAAP and non-GAAP pictures diverge materially. Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 45% and non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.98; the non-GAAP measures exclude stock-based compensation, amortization of acquired intangibles and non-recurring items. Full-year guidance shows the same split, with GAAP EPS of $5.76 to $5.90 and non-GAAP EPS of $7.74 to $7.88. Margin expansion is real on both bases, but readers should value the business on GAAP earnings with that gap in mind.
financials.balanceCommentary:
The balance sheet is simple. Cash and short-term investments stood at $0.3B at FY25 year-end and total equity at $0.6B. The vendor table shows no figure for total debt or net debt in any year; we treat that as missing data rather than confirmed zero, and the Facts carry no interest-coverage figure either.

The TTM current ratio of 1.38 looks modest for a cash-generative software company. The MD&A explains why that number says less here than usual: Qualys bills the full subscription upfront and holds it as deferred revenue until earned, so a large part of current liabilities is service owed to customers rather than cash owed to lenders. We see no balance-sheet constraint on the business; the risk sits in revenue growth, not in the funding structure.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
FCF margin was 45.5% in FY25, but it has swung over the five years shown, dipping to 37.5% in FY22 and 38.1% in FY24, so a single year's figure is not a trend. Capital expenditure is negligible, consistent with a hosted subscription model.

Q2'26 operating cash flow rose {+ 77% +} to $59.6 million from $33.8 million. The press release gives no cause, and with upfront annual billing, quarterly cash flow can swing on invoicing timing; we would not extrapolate one quarter.

Share repurchases absorb a large part of free cash flow every year in the table and there is no dividend; how well that cash is deployed is discussed under Management.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing numbers the shares trade at 33.4x P/E, 24.8x EV/EBITDA and 9.5x sales, with a 4.7% FCF yield. Forward, the multiple is 24.7x NTM earnings and ~22.8x FY27E, on consensus EPS of $7.81 for FY26E and $8.45 for FY27E.

The consensus EPS basis is unstated. The FY26E consensus figure sits inside the company's non-GAAP guidance of $7.74 to $7.88 and well above GAAP guidance of $5.76 to $5.90, so the forward multiples appear to be non-GAAP-based and flatter the stock against the GAAP trailing P/E. No peer multiples are available, so we cannot say whether the stock is cheap or expensive relative to the group.

The Street is less positive than the price. The consensus target of $179.36 and median of $177.50 both sit below the current price, against a $130.00–$220.00 range of individual targets. A stock this close to its 52-week high, with only 4 Buy ratings out of 22, has to deliver upside surprises to move higher. We use the Street range to anchor our Bull and Bear cases.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Set at the $220.00 top of the Street target range. Requires the reacceleration management describes: Q3 revenue above the guided range, federal wins following FedRAMP High, and QFlex and Enterprise TruRisk Management converting into faster growth, so the market pays more than today's FY27E multiple.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The current ~22.8x multiple on FY27E consensus EPS of $8.45 holds, which is today's price. Revenue lands inside the raised $732.0–$738.0 million guide, growth stays in the guided 9% to 10% band, and margins hold near Q2 levels.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Set at the $130.00 bottom of the Street target range. Growth slips below the guide as extended sales cycles and price competition bite, the fixed cost base the 10-K describes stops margins expanding, and the market re-rates the stock toward the most cautious analyst's view.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries 55% because the Q2 print and the guidance raise support the current run-rate, and nothing in the filing points to an inflection in either direction. Bull at 25% is slightly heavier than Bear at 20%: management has just raised guidance and margins are still widening, while the Bear path requires several things together, a revenue miss and a de-rating, rather than any one of them.

The weighting leaves expected value slightly below the current price and Bear downside well beyond the 15% floor, which is why the rating is HOLD rather than BUY. Our $180–$205 target range brackets the Base case and spans a narrow band either side of today's price.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Qualys reports a single reportable segment, so FY25 revenue of $669.1M is the whole business; the vendor provides no product or regional split. The revenue base is subscriptions to the Qualys Cloud Apps on the Enterprise TruRisk Platform, spanning vulnerability management, asset management, patch management, policy compliance, endpoint detection and response, and the TotalCloud cloud-security suite. Growth, per the MD&A, comes from existing customers renewing and buying additional subscriptions and from new customers.

moatFactors.name: Platform breadth on a single agent
moatFactors.body: The press release describes the platform as leveraging a single agent across on-premises, endpoint, cloud, container and mobile assets, and the MD&A pitches a single platform for IT, security, application, endpoint, developer and cloud teams. Each additional app a customer adds on that agent raises the cost of switching. The counterweight is the 10-K's own description of a market with short product life cycles and frequent new product introductions.

moatFactors.name: Recurring, prepaid subscriptions
moatFactors.body: Mostly one-year renewable subscriptions, invoiced upfront and recognized ratably, give revenue visibility and fund the business ahead of delivery. The gross margin trend (see Financials) suggests pricing has held so far. Annual terms also mean customers can leave at each renewal, and the 10-K lists changes in customer renewals among the drivers of results.

moatFactors.name: Government authorization
moatFactors.body: TotalCloud's FedRAMP High Authorization extends the Qualys Government Platform and opens the FedRAMP Marketplace to federal agencies. Authorizations take effort to obtain, which can deter smaller entrants, but the press release lists maintaining them as a risk, and the federal revenue benefit is not yet visible in reported figures.

moatFactors.name: Cloud and channel integration
moatFactors.body: The press release says Qualys integrates its vulnerability management capabilities into offerings from Amazon Web Services, the Google Cloud Platform and Microsoft Azure, and the company generates a significant portion of sales through channel partners. That reach lowers customer acquisition friction, though partners are also a dependency the MD&A names as a forward-looking risk.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Margin expansion in each year from FY21 to FY25 points to real customer stickiness and pricing discipline. The limit is the market structure the 10-K describes: rapid technological advances, customer price sensitivity and intense competition, any of which could pressure pricing, gross margins and renewal rates. A wide moat would show up as growth holding or accelerating while margins widen; so far the record shows margins widening while growth settled near 10%. The signal to watch is whether gross margin keeps rising as the company pushes newer products such as TotalCloud and Enterprise TruRisk Management.

points: **Guidance raised, but the slope is flat.** The 2026 revenue guide now implies 9% to 10% growth over 2025, close to FY25's pace. Against that, the Q3 guide carries the same range, below Q2's 11%, so the second half is guided slower.

**Street models steady growth.** Consensus sees FY26E revenue of ~$735.1M and FY27E of $795.5M, near the middle of the company's range and implying no step change. A move in FY27 estimates, not the FY26 guide, is what would shift the valuation debate.

**Federal opening.** TotalCloud's FedRAMP High Authorization makes the cloud suite available to federal agencies, and the CEO cites a growing federal pipeline. No federal revenue figure is disclosed, so the size of the opportunity cannot be checked yet.

**AI positioning.** Management frames its innovation as AI for security and security for AI, and cites collaborations with Anthropic Project Glasswing and Open AI's Trusted Access for Cyber program. These are positioning, not revenue; the 10-Q lists AI among the technology trends its forward-looking statements depend on.

**New offers.** The CEO points to growing AI-native Risk Operations Center adoption on Enterprise TruRisk Management and promising early QFlex engagement, and the Converge joint offering links ETM use to potentially lower cyber insurance premiums. None of these has a disclosed revenue contribution, so we treat them as options on reacceleration rather than part of the Base case.

management.leadership: The 2026 proxy statement (filed April 22, 2026) names Sumedh S. Thakar as Director, President and Chief Executive Officer, Joo Mi Kim as Chief Financial Officer and Bruce K. Posey as Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary. The proxy excerpt does not give their tenures. In the August 4, 2026 earnings press release, Mr. Thakar described the quarter as continued solid execution and expressed confidence in reaccelerating long-term growth. That confidence has not yet reached the guidance, which still implies 9% to 10% growth, so we treat it as a stated aim rather than evidence.
management.capitalAllocation:
Qualys pays no dividend and returns cash through repurchases. FY25 share repurchases totaled $183.4M. Free cash flow of $304.4M that year covered them with room to spare, and repurchases appear as a cash outflow in each year of the five-year table. The MD&A lists the share repurchase program and acquisitions among its anticipated uses of capital, without detail in the excerpt.

The share count is hard to track from the sources available: the proxy reports 35,289,949 shares outstanding at April 14, 2026, while the vendor snapshot derives ~34.59M from market cap; we use the proxy figure as the company's own count. Buybacks at a forward multiple in the low twenties are a reasonable use of surplus cash for a cash-generative company growing at the guided pace, but they return less per dollar the higher the share price; we would rather see the pace flex with valuation.
management.governance:
Per the April 22, 2026 proxy, the board has determined six directors to be independent: Mr. Berquist, Mr. Brooks, Mr. Hank, Ms. Pfeiffer, Ms. Rogers and Dr. Zangardi. Mr. Hank, an independent non-employee director, has chaired the board since January 2023, with the CEO and Chair roles separate. In 2025 the board met 4 times and the Audit and Risk Committee 8 times.

Executive pay ties annual cash incentives to bookings, revenue growth and non-GAAP EPS, and PRSUs to revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA margin; cash awards are capped at 125% of target. The use of non-GAAP metrics means stock-based compensation does not count against the pay targets, which is worth watching given the GAAP gap discussed under Financials.

The one disclosed related-person item is modest: the CEO's sister, Deepti S. Thakar, earned $248,282 as a Product Director in 2025, reviewed and approved or ratified by the Audit and Risk Committee. We see a conventional, independent-led board with no structural concern for outside holders.
management.insiderOwnership: As of April 14, 2026, per the proxy, each named executive officer and director owned less than 1% of the shares, and all current directors and executive officers as a group held 255,155 shares, also below 1%. The CEO's beneficial holding was 155,940 shares. The two holders above 5% are BlackRock, Inc. at 14.4% and The Vanguard Group at 11.8%; neither stake amounts to control. With no controlling holder and small insider stakes, outside shareholders' alignment with management rests mainly on the equity-heavy pay design rather than on ownership.

idiosyncratic: **Growth stalls below the guide.** The Base case assumes 9% to 10% growth; the Q3 guide already steps down from Q2's pace. A revenue miss would hit a stock priced above the Street's consensus target and would likely compress the multiple as well as estimates. Watch Q3 revenue against the guided range and the calculated current billings the company publishes for modelers.

**Price competition.** The 10-K describes customer price sensitivity and intense competition that could create downward pressure on pricing and gross margins and hurt renewal rates. Because gross margin expansion underpins the margin story, watch gross margin (83.3% TTM) for an early sign of pricing pressure.

**Operating leverage cuts both ways.** The 10-K states that a significant percentage of operating expenses are fixed and that the company generally cannot offset revenue shortfalls by cutting costs in the short term. A growth miss would therefore show up in operating margin quickly. Watch GAAP operating margin against the 34% of Q2'26.

**GAAP versus non-GAAP gap.** Pay targets and the apparent basis of consensus EPS are non-GAAP, while stock-based compensation and acquisition amortization are real costs to shareholders. If the gap widens, GAAP earnings growth will lag the headline. Watch the spread between GAAP and non-GAAP EPS guidance each quarter.

**Federal dependence on authorizations.** Part of the reacceleration case rests on federal demand, and the press release lists the ability to maintain government authorizations as a risk. Losing or delaying an authorization would stall that pipeline. Watch for disclosed federal wins and any change to FedRAMP status.
risks.systemic: The 10-Q MD&A flags inflationary pressure, high interest rates, significant volatility of global markets, reduced spending and extended sales cycles, tariff and non-tariff trade barriers, and geopolitical conflicts as factors that could cause customers to reduce or eliminate IT security spending. The 10-K adds foreign currency movements and changes in regulation as sources of variability in results. Security spending has defensive qualities, but a stock trading at a premium forward multiple is exposed to a broader de-rating of software valuations regardless of company execution. Watch the Q3 commentary on sales cycles and deal timing.

body: **HOLD, target range $180–$205.** Qualys is a high-quality, cash-generative subscription business that executed well in Q2'26 and raised guidance. The guidance still describes a company growing around 10%, and the share price sits above the Street's central view, so we see the risk-reward as balanced rather than attractive.

We would turn more constructive on two kinds of evidence: reported revenue growth moving above the guided band, with federal and newer-product contributions visible, or a share price closer to the low end of our target range without a change in fundamentals. A revenue miss against the Q3 guide, or gross margin starting to slip, would move us toward the Bear case.
